title: Beyond Lung-Protective: APRV, Recruitment, Intraoperative PEEP
keywords: Tlow terminate at 50-75% peak expiratory flow
Plow 0 does not mean zero PEEP
IMPROVE low tidal volume PROVHILO no benefit high PEEP RM
sources: Critical Vector — Vent Pocket Guide: APRV, Recruitment, Intraoperative Protective Ventilation
ART trial (JAMA 2017); IMPROVE (NEJM 2013); PROVHILO (Lancet 2014); APRV/BiVent meta-analysis 2026

changelog.change: Initial entry — APRV four-parameter setup + titration, judicious recruitment technique + decremental PEEP trial, and the OR protective-ventilation evidence.

summary: Three related topics past the standard lung-protective bundle. APRV setup varies more across centres than any other mode. Aggressive maximal recruitment (ART: PEEP 45, peak 60) caused harm — a moderate staircase manoeuvre plus a decremental PEEP trial is a different thing. In the routine surgical patient, low tidal volume does the work; added PEEP/recruitment mostly adds haemodynamic cost.

rows: Set to the Pplat from the prior conventional mode; do not exceed 30 cmH₂O

Commonly 0 — this does NOT create zero PEEP: the release time is too brief for full emptying, so meaningful intrinsic PEEP persists. Raising P low above 0 unpredictably changes both intrinsic PEEP and delivered VT
4–6 s with reasonably preserved lungs; a longer T high improves oxygenation
The most consequential and least standardised — commonly set to terminate the release at 50–75% of the peak expiratory flow, targeting ~ 10–14 releases/min

items: Hypoxaemia: raise P high and/or T high (and FiO₂) first.
Hypercapnia: shorten T high to increase release frequency, or lighten sedation to allow more spontaneous breathing — spontaneous effort is central to how APRV works, not incidental.

Evidence (2026 meta-analysis, 9 studies, ~1900 patients): APRV/BiVent improved oxygenation and ventilator-free days vs conventional ventilation, with no mortality benefit. Treat any single centre's protocol as one implementation among several.

rows: Step PEEP up in stages (e.g. 4→10 for a few breaths, 10→15, 15→20 held longer), peak capped ~ 40–50 cmH₂O — well below ART's 60
After the manoeuvre, step PEEP down (e.g. by 2 every few minutes) watching oxygenation and compliance; the lowest PEEP before benefit is lost, plus a small margin, is the working PEEP

body.text: ART's harm signal was about the technique and magnitude (sustained 45–60 cmH₂O), not the concept of recruitment. Still: abort any manoeuvre for hypotension or new desaturation, avoid it in hypovolaemia / right-heart failure / a known bronchopleural fistula, and only recruit lungs that are recruitable (diffuse ARDS, early, high P/F response).

rows: Major abdominal surgery — VT 6–8 mL/kg PBW + PEEP 6–8 + recruitment q30min vs VT 10–12, no PEEP: the protective strategy reduced major pulmonary and extrapulmonary complications

Both arms already low-VT — high PEEP (12) + recruitment vs low PEEP (≤ 2), no recruitment: no difference in pulmonary complications; the high-PEEP arm had more intraoperative hypotension and vasopressor use

body.text: Read together: the low tidal volume is doing the real work. In the routine open-abdominal population, PEEP and recruitment added on top add haemodynamic cost without a demonstrated benefit — a mirror of the ART pattern in a lower-acuity population. Later trials (PROBESE in obesity, iPROVE-OLV in one-lung ventilation) suggest PEEP/recruitment may still matter in specific subgroups; that is unsettled.
